# Palette

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Imaging` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class Palette
```

The palette a painting front-end offers: [`Palette.Slots`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.Palette.md#f-slots) ramp entries that change with the [`PaletteMode`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.PaletteMode.md), plus the rules for the swatches a user saves beside them.

It lives in Core, not in a front-end, for the same reason `VariantPreview` does: the CLI and the GUI must agree on what "the fifth gray" is, and two copies is how that stops being true. The ramps are also *computed* rather than typed out, so the grays are reproducible and evenly spaced by construction instead of by whoever transcribed them.

Both ramps are exactly [`Palette.Slots`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.Palette.md#f-slots) long, and swapping the mode reuses the same ten slots — the palette's shape never changes, only its contents.

## Properties

### GrayRamp { #p-grayramp }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<RgbColor> GrayRamp { get; }
```

Ten ascending grays from black to white, evenly spaced across the full 0..255 range.

Both endpoints are included — unlike the half-open ranges `ColorRoller` samples, this is a fixed ten-entry table rather than a sampled interval, and a gray ramp that could not reach white would be missing the color authors reach for most.

### RainbowRamp { #p-rainbowramp }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<RgbColor> RainbowRamp { get; }
```

Ten fully saturated hues spread evenly around the wheel, starting at red.

The step is 360/10, and the last slot is 324° rather than 360°: 360 wraps to 0, so including it would spend two of the ten slots on the same red.

The two palette scopes resolved into one list: the open CookBook's swatches first, the app-wide ones beneath, with anything present in both appearing once, at its book position.

**Parameters**

- `book` (`IEnumerable<RgbColor>?`) - The open CookBook's swatches, or null when no book is open — in which case the app palette is all there is.
- `app` (`IEnumerable<RgbColor>?`) - The app-wide swatches from the `.nfty` store.

**Returns.** The combined list, in precedence order.

### FromSpecs(IEnumerable&lt;string?&gt;?) { #m-fromspecs-system-collections-generic-ienumerable-system-string }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<RgbColor> FromSpecs(IEnumerable<string?>? specs);
```

Reads swatches out of the prefixed color specs a manifest or a store file holds.

An entry that will not parse is SKIPPED rather than thrown on. A palette is convenience state — one mangled swatch must never be the reason a CookBook cannot be opened — and the same read has to survive a hand-edited manifest. Anything that must reject a bad spec loudly should call [`ColorSpec.Parse()`](../nfty-ticket/Nfty.Core.Imaging.ColorSpec.md#m-parse-system-string) itself.

**Parameters**

- `specs` (`IEnumerable<string?>?`) - Prefixed specs (`hex:`, `rgb:`, `hsl:`, `hsv:`), or null.

**Returns.** The colors that parsed, in order.

### InMode(IEnumerable&lt;RgbColor&gt;?, PaletteMode) { #m-inmode-system-collections-generic-ienumerable-nfty-cor-5487db }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<RgbColor> InMode(IEnumerable<RgbColor>? colors, PaletteMode mode);
```

The swatches that belong to a mode's palette.

**Parameters**

- `colors` (`IEnumerable<RgbColor>?`) - Swatches from a source that records no mode.
- `mode` (`PaletteMode`) - The mode being offered.

**Returns.** The swatches that belong in that mode, in order.

**Remarks**

**The two palettes are separate, and the rule is the color itself.** Grayscale mode paints a value-map, where a color has no meaning beyond its lightness: a saved vermilion offered there is a cell that silently arms a mid gray, and a row of twenty of them is twenty cells the author cannot tell apart. Color mode has the opposite problem — the grays a value-map is authored in are the least useful entries in a rainbow.

Saving always writes to the palette for the mode in force, so a grayscale palette can only ever contain grays by construction. This is for the swatches that arrive carrying no mode at all: a CookBook's own palette, which travels in its archive. Routing them by GRAYNESS is the only answer that needs no stored field and agrees with what saving would have done.
